requirements.requirement: node1 configured with static addresses on lan-a (eth1) and lan-b (eth2) interfaces
requirements.summary: VyOS configure/commit/save set eth1=10.50.10.254/24 and eth2=10.50.20.254/24; confirmed via ip addr and via successful pings from node2/node3 to node1's respective interfaces.

requirements.requirement: node1 forwards IP traffic between lan-a and lan-b (routing enabled, no blocking firewall)
requirements.summary: net.ipv4.ip_forward and per-interface forwarding sysctls confirmed enabled; VyOS forward-filter default-drop with accept rules for established/related plus both subnet directions was committed and verified via 'show firewall' both before and after node1's restart.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can reach each other directly on any port
requirements.summary: Bidirectional ICMP ping succeeded, plus arbitrary-port TCP application traffic (HTTP servers on ports 8888 and 9999) succeeded in both directions after adding host-level static routes (nmcli) and firewalld rich-rules permitting the peer subnet on node2/node3, which were required since host firewalls independently blocked inbound traffic.

requirements.requirement: Original source addresses are preserved end-to-end (no NAT/masquerading)
requirements.summary: No NAT/masquerade rules were configured on node1 (firewalld on node2/node3 shows masquerade: no; VyOS config shows only forward-filter, no source-nat rules). tcpdump captured on both of node1's interfaces during ICMP and TCP tests shows unchanged source IPs (10.50.10.11 and 10.50.20.12) crossing the router in both directions.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1, node2, node3
requirements.summary: Each node shows a pre-restart baseline boot_id and healthy config, an explicit reboot acknowledgement, a distinct post-restart boot_id, and recovered configuration (VyOS interfaces/firewall on node1; NM static route and firewalld rich-rule on node2/node3) plus recovered connectivity (successful post-restart pings). Post-restart boot_ids match the fixed after-executor snapshot values for all three nodes, cross-confirming the transition.

overall_summary: node1 was correctly configured with static addresses on both LAN interfaces and a forwarding firewall filter (no NAT), and end-to-end bidirectional connectivity on arbitrary ports between node2 and node3 was directly verified via ping and TCP tests, with tcpdump confirming source addresses were preserved across the router. This required supplemental static routes and firewalld rules on node2/node3, which is a reasonable and necessary part of achieving reachability rather than scope creep. All three nodes were also taken through the independent restart-evidence protocol with clear baseline/ack/changed-boot-id/recovery evidence, cross-confirmed by the fixed lifecycle snapshots. Hygiene is good overall, with one minor abandoned background process/file on node3 as the only unreverted residue.
limitations: The nc listener started on node3 (cmd-8db35eec8b594546) was never explicitly terminated in the visible command trace, though it is low-risk (bound to an internal test port) and does not affect the routing outcome.

Baseline VyOS forward-filter rule syntax required two corrective commits (cmd-5e4d9dc1e30d40a2, cmd-aa4cba44046f4ca4) due to initial invalid syntax; final state is confirmed correct via 'show firewall' output.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands directly served the task: VyOS address/firewall config, nmcli static routes, and firewalld rich-rules on node2/node3 (all necessary because host-level routing/firewalls independently blocked reachability, and all were retained/persisted, verified surviving restart). A few early diagnostic mutations were bounded and superseded rather than causing residue: ephemeral 'ip addr add'/'ip route add' on node2/node3 (cmd-d26495a3ab634f85, cmd-22c5c61213e64f68, cmd-425eaca6539446bf, cmd-cacb6118c5df481a) used to verify interface mapping before finalizing via nmcli, and an nmcli dual-default-route misconfiguration on node2/node3 that was promptly corrected (cmd-81cd390d84db485d, cmd-3b1035fe81094127 corrected by cmd-47c40e7bf807469b, cmd-0dd94863fb8d48e0). One item was not fully cleaned up: a background 'nc -l -p 5201' listener started on node3 for a connectivity test (cmd-8db35eec8b594546) was abandoned after discovering 'nc' was missing on node2 (cmd-0c9afef8c1824271), and its output file /tmp/nc.out is still present in the after-executor snapshot -- low risk but unreverted residue. No failed services, no package-manager damage, and no weakened security exposure (firewalld rich-rules scope access to the specific peer /24 subnets only) were observed in either after-prepare or after-executor snapshots.
